experimental_procedure: (S)-tert-Butyl-4-formyl-2,2-dimethyloxazolidine-3-carboxylate (3). A solution of N-Boc-( S)-serine methyl ester (12.0 g, 46.3 mmol) in toluene (100 mL) was cooled to -78 °C under nitrogen. To the cooled solution was slowly added DIBAL-H (83 mL, a 1.5 M solution in toluene). The reaction mixture was stirred for 2 h at -78 °C, and the reaction was quenched by slowly adding 100 mL of cold MeOH. The resulting white emulsion was slowly poured into 200 mL of ice-cold 1 M HCl with swirling over 20 min, and the aqueous mixture was extracted with EtOAc (3 x 120 mL). The combined organic layers were washed with brine (150 mL), dried (Na2SO4), and concentrated to give the crude product as a colorless oil, which was vacuum distilled to provide aldehyde 3 (7.5 g, 71%) as a colorless liquid. bp 115-125 °C (9.0 mm Hg).

Oxalyl chloride (240 μL, 2.75 mmol) was added dropwise to a slurry of octahydroisoquinoline-4-carboxylicAcid derivatives (320 mg, 1.36 mmol) in benzene (6.8 mL) and the mixture was stirred for 5 h. The solvent was removed under reduced pressure (water aspirator with drying tube), the residue was redissolved in benzene (6 mL) and the solution was concentrated. The resulting green residue was dissolved in CH2Cl2 (6.8mL) and the solution was immediately cooled to -78 °C. Diisobutylaluminum hydride (1.5 mL of a 1.0 M solution in toluene, 1.5 mmol) was added dropwise and the solution was warmed to 0 °C over 1.5 h. The solution was returned to -78 °C and an additional 1.1 equiv of diisobutylaluminum hydride (1.5 mL of a 1.0 M solution in toluene, 1.5 mmol) was added dropwise. The solution was warmed to 0 °C over 1 h and then cooled to -78 °C as EtOAc (0.5 mL) was added to quench excess hydride reagent. After 5 min, the cold bath was removed and Rochelle's salt solution (10%, 20 mL) was added. The mixture was stirred vigorously for 4 h and extracted with CH2Cl2 (4 x 20 mL). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General method for the synthesis of aldehyde derivatives. The methyl ester was dissolved in distilled diethyl ether (0.2 M) and the resulting solution was placed under a nitrogen atmosphere. This solution and diisobutyl aluminium hydride (DIBAL) (3 equiv) in diethyl ether (0.6 M) was cooled in a -78 °C acetone-dry ice bath. The DIBAL solution was cannula transferred to the methyl ester solution and the solution was stirred for 1 h. At -78 °C, methanol (equal to half of the diethyl ether by volume) was added, and then 15 equiv of acetic acid was added. The reaction mixture was stirred for 5 min and then transferred to an ice bath, and saturated sodium tartrate solution (equal to the volume of diethyl ether) was added. The aqueous layer was extracted three times with ethyl acetate. The organic washes were combined and extracted once with water. The organic layer was dried with anhydrous sodium sulfate and the solvent was removed under reduced pressure. experimental_procedure: The methyl ester (48 mg, 0.12 mmol, 1 equiv) was dissolved in 0.54 mL of distilled diethyl ether and put under a nitrogen atmosphere. This solution and diisobutyl aluminium hydride (DIBAL) (57 μL, 0.32 mmol, 3 equiv) in 0.54 mL of diethyl ether was cooled in a -78 °C acetone-dry ice bath. The DIBAL solution was cannula transferred to the methyl ester solution and the solution was stirred for 1 h. At -78 °C, methanol (equal to half of the diethyl ether by volume) was added, and then 15 equiv of acetic acid was added. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General method for the synthesis of aldehyde derivatives. The methyl ester was dissolved in distilled diethyl ether (0.2 M) and the resulting solution was placed under a nitrogen atmosphere. The DIBAL solution was cannula transferred to the methyl ester solution and the solution was stirred for 1 h. At -78 °C, methanol (equal to half of the diethyl ether by volume) was added, and then 15 equiv of acetic acid was added. The aqueous layer was extracted three times with ethyl acetate. The organic washes were combined and extracted once with water. authors: Bajwa, Naval; Jennings, Michael P.
reference: Efficient and Selective Reduction Protocols of the 2,2-Dimethyl-1,3-benzodioxan-4-one Functional Group to Readily Provide Both Substituted Salicylaldehydes and 2-Hydroxybenzyl Alcohols | Bajwa, Naval; Jennings, Michael P. | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2006), 71(9), 3646-3649
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the Preparation of Aldehydes 3a-3l. A solution of substituted 2,2-dimethyl-1,3-benzodioxan-4-one (1 mmol) in CH2Cl2 at -78 °C was treated with DIBAL-H (3 mmol, 1 M solution in CH2Cl2). The reaction mixture was stirred at -78 °C for 2 h and then quenched with 1 M HCl and MeOH. After warming to room temperature, H2O was added, and the aqueous layer was extracted three times with Et2O. The combined organic layers were washed with water and brine, dried with MgSO4, and concentrated in vacuo. Chromatography on silica gel with hexanes- EtOAc (95:5) as the eluent afforded the targeted aldehyde compounds 3a-3j.
notes: chemoselective, optimization study, optimized on reagent, toluene/solvent gave lower yield

Garner's methyl ester (10) of >95% purity was prepared from L-serine in three steps from a literature procedure.44 The reactors were constructed according to Scheme 6 and consisted of a cooled reactor assembly equipped with three reagent precooling PFA loops of 0.4 mL volume, a PFA reactor coil of 10 mL volume, and a 0.4 mL cooled PFA quench loop. This reactor assembly was maintained at -70 °C. In series with this reactor was a PFA reactor coil of 2 mL volume at ambient temperature (23-26 °C) and a back-pressure regulator with a 6 bar limit. A solution of diisobutylaluminium hydride (DIBAL-H), 1.0 M nominal concentration in hexane, was plugged into line B. The three pumps were begun, pumping solvent at the indicated flow rates for 5 min.
